attributions.claim: Walker measured knee kinematics and applied the results to prosthesis design across several decades, which connected the two literatures more directly than most work did.
Freeman and Swanson designed and reported an early total knee replacement in the 1970s, and argued the case for a particular balance between constraint and fixation.
Insall and colleagues developed the total condylar prosthesis in the same period, which became the pattern most modern designs descend from.
Goodfellow and O'Connor designed and reported the meniscal bearing unicompartmental knee, arguing from contact mechanics for a mobile bearing.
Banks and Hodge measured implanted knee kinematics with fluoroscopy, which made it possible to see what a prosthesis does in a living loaded knee rather than on a rig.
Dennis and Komistek used in vivo fluoroscopic measurement to describe paradoxical anterior translation of the femur during flexion in many implanted knees.
Bellemans and colleagues measured alignment in a healthy population in the 2010s and described constitutional varus, which challenged that target.
Bourne and colleagues reported patient satisfaction after knee arthroplasty from a large cohort, which separated satisfaction from surgical success as outcomes.
Patient reported outcome and satisfaction entered the field as endpoints, and the satisfaction figure changed how consent is taken more than it changed how the operation is done.
